# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences heart-related issues, including a familial history of cardiac issues and regular heart check-ups to monitor her heart health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation issues, which can be frustrating at times. Managing her diet and ensuring she stays hydrated helps alleviate these issues somewhat, but it's an ongoing challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, which affects her muscle tone. This condition makes her muscles feel stiffer than they should be, and she is working with therapists to manage its impact on her daily life.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hypotonia is a common feature of KBG syndrome, affecting muscle tone and leading to stiffness.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities requiring close monitoring with her healthcare team.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Palatal abnormalities are a common feature of KBG syndrome, potentially impacting speech and feeding.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences vision problems such as astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia/hypermetropia), with occasional squinting (strabismus) and hearing concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems, including astigmatism and short-sightedness, are common in KBG syndrome, while hearing concerns can lead to speech delays.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly with cold foods, indicating potential dental issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Tooth sensitivity is a common complaint among people with KBG syndrome, especially with cold or hot foods.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and challenges in reaching certain milestones, requiring additional support and accommodations in her education.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have developmental delays, including difficulties in reaching milestones and experiencing challenges in school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety, and requires medication in some cases.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences, including ASD, ADHD, and anxiety, are common in KBG syndrome, and some individuals may require additional support or treatment.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th finger (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal abnormalities, including an increased curvature of the spine and short fingers, are common in KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screen for hearing issues: Regular hearing checks starting at age 5.
b) Screen for vision issues: Regular eye exams, particularly focusing on astigmatism and short-sightedness.
c) Screen for heart issues: Regular heart check-ups to monitor heart health.
d) Screen for digestive issues: Monitoring for constipation and managing dietary intake.
e) Screen for dental issues: Regular dental check-ups to address tooth sensitivity.
f) Screen for neurological issues: Working with therapists to manage muscle tone and other associated symptoms.
g) Screen for palatal issues: Close monitoring with healthcare providers to address palatal abnormalities.
h) Screen for heart valve issues: Regular echocardiograms and ECGs to monitor heart health.
i) Screen for hormonal imbalances: N/A.
j) Screen for immune system issues: N/A.
k) Screen for gastrointestinal issues: Monitoring for constipation and managing dietary intake.
l) Screen for cardiac issues: Regular heart check-ups to monitor heart health.
m) Screen for tethered cord: MRI scans to rule out complications, particularly sacral dimples.
n) Screen for palatal issues: Close monitoring with healthcare providers to address palatal abnormalities.
